Row.Text: Word has come to the Bulgar court of an old shepherd’s struggle with his neighbors’ claim to his pasture. They sent their livestock to graze in his land; he drove them off. They sought to buy his land; he refused to sell. In court, they argued their right to his land; he refused to leave. They poisoned his well; he drank rain water. They burned his barn; he rebuilt it. The story is becoming quite popular.
Bulgaria should have more men like these. Make a role and position for them.
The man is clearly an idiot. Why did he not move?

In a quiet meeting corner, a foreign diplomat hisses at his Bulgarian counterpart: “Why can’t you just cooperate?” The Bulgarian gives a smile that does not reach his eyes, and shrugs. Bulgaria persists in being Bulgarian.
Perhaps Bulgarian diplomats could be more… diplomatic.
